questions.question: Why did gross margin fall in the West region in Q3 2026?
questions.answer: West gross margin fell mainly because Calder Metals' unit cost rose sharply, not because discounts increased. COGS increased $4.74m while revenue increased $0.87m; Metals contributed $4.22m of COGS increase through price effect and $0.78m through mix. Discount dollars declined. Basis: completed West order lines, Q2 versus Q3 2026.

questions.question: Metals profitability got worse in the third quarter of 2026. Why?
questions.answer: Metals profitability worsened because unit costs rose sharply across the sole supplier, Calder Metals, without enough price recovery. Gross margin fell from 31.1% in Q2 to 18.7% in Q3; gross profit dropped $5.10M despite higher revenue. questions.question: Was the Q2 2026 rise in discounting spread across all segments or concentrated?
questions.answer: Discount dollars rose across all segments, but rate increase was concentrated in SMB. Enterprise drove most added discount dollars; SMB discount rate jumped from 3.99% to 11.05%, while Enterprise barely rose and Mid-Market dipped. Based on completed-order lines, comparing Q2 2026 with Q1 2026; rate means discount as share of pre-discount sales.

questions.question: Which group of customers started paying well after the due date in 2026?
questions.answer: No segment, on average. In 2026, Enterprise and Mid-Market averaged 1.1 days early; SMB averaged 1.5 days early. Still, Mid-Market had 40 invoices and Enterprise 39 paid 30+ days late (SMB: 24). Each segment had zero 30+ day-late payments in 2025, so those long delays emerged in 2026, but no group paid late overall on average.
